summary: A classic Thai dessert of ripe mango with coconut-sweetened glutinous rice and coconut cream. Bangkok has established shops serving it year-round, but December falls outside the main Thai mango harvest, so fruit quality and availability are less predictable than in the March–May peak.
whyGo: A compact, memorable way to try the contrast of fragrant mango, rich coconut rice and salty coconut cream.
K. Panich in the Old Town is a longstanding family shop; Mae Varee in Thonglor lists two mango varieties and long daily hours.
bestFor: Travelers seeking a famous Thai dessert and a light snack after a meal.
Visitors who can be flexible about mango size, ripeness and seasonal quality.
skipIf: You are planning a special trip specifically for peak-season mango; March–May is a better target.
You need guaranteed December availability or have a coconut allergy; confirm ingredients and cross-contact with the vendor.
duration: Allow 20–40 minutes for a simple stop, including a queue; this is a planning estimate and excludes travel between neighborhoods.
cost: No current menu price was confirmed. Budget roughly ฿80–180 per serving as a planning estimate; premium or hotel versions can cost more.
hours: K. Panich is listed by Michelin and Time Out as open Monday–Saturday, 07:00–17:00, closed Sunday. Time Out lists Mae Varee as daily 06:00–22:00. Recheck shortly before visiting.
bestTime: Try in the morning or early afternoon, while shops are open and before popular vendors sell out. For the best chance of peak mango flavor, visit during March–May rather than December.
gettingThere: Choose one shop rather than crossing town for the dish. K. Panich is at 431–433 Tanao Road in Phra Nakhon; taxi or ride-hail is practical for the Old Town. Mae Varee is at 1 Thonglor, near Thong Lo BTS. Check live traffic and the route on the day.
booking: No reservation is normally needed for a takeaway dessert stop. K. Panich has a separate dine-in space across the street according to Michelin; call ahead if you need seating or want to confirm December stock (+66 2 221 3554).
accessibility: Accessibility details are not published in the sources reviewed. These are small street-side shops; ask about step-free entry, seating and restroom access before making a dedicated trip.
practicalTips: Ask whether ripe mango is available before joining a queue; availability and quality are more uncertain outside the harvest peak.
Eat soon after purchase: sticky rice is best warm or freshly prepared, and cut mango does not travel well in Bangkok heat.
If K. Panich is closed on Sunday, Mae Varee is listed as open daily; verify both listings before setting out.
decemberNotes: December 2026 is outside the Department of Agricultural Extension's listed March–May peak period for Thai mango. Year-round shop listings do not guarantee the same mango varieties or quality in December; ask on the day and treat the dish as a bonus rather than a fixed seasonal highlight. No dated December food event was found.
uncertainties: December 2026 stock, mango variety, ripeness and prices are not published this far ahead.
Opening hours are current listings, not a guarantee against holiday changes or temporary closure.
Step-free access and other accessibility details were not confirmed.
